question: The marked price of a calculator is Rs. 1200. It is sold at a discount of 25 percent. If the cost price of the calculator is Rs. 800, then what is the value of profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) is (100 − 25)% of Marked Price (MP).

SP = 75% of 1200 = 3/4 × 1200 = Rs. 900.

Profit = SP − CP = 900 − 800 = Rs. 100.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP: 800
 
 SP: 900
 
 MP: 1200
 

 Profit = +100
 

 Discount = 25%
 Profit = SP − CP = 100

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 1200

Discount = 25%

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 800

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − Discount / 100)

Profit = SP − CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 1200 × (100 − 25) / 100

⇒ SP = 1200 × 75 / 100

⇒ SP = 12 × 75 = Rs. 900

⇒ Profit = 900 − 800

⇒ Profit = Rs. 100

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the article. Formula: Discount = MP − SP.

Profit & Loss Calculation

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP). Formula: Profit% = (Profit / CP) × 100.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the equivalent discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) / 100.
